response.consequence: After a save or any background refetch that changes the data, the form unmounts and remounts. The user sees a flicker and loses unsaved edits and the current tab state. The extra reset and refetch also add redundant network requests.
response.explanation: The effect's cleanup invalidates and resets the event-type query. It was meant to run only on unmount or when `id` changed. The change adds `eventTypeQueryData` to the dependency array, so the cleanup now runs whenever the fetched data changes. Examples are a refetch after saving, a window-focus refetch, or the first load after an earlier reset. Each time, the old render's cleanup sees truthy data and calls resetQueries. That clears the data to undefined, so `if (!eventTypeQueryData) return null` unmounts the whole EventType form until the refetch returns.
response.title: Adding eventTypeQueryData to effect deps resets the query on every data change

response.consequence: On Linux, a developer with an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL line keeps a stale tunnel URL, while the script claims it was updated. Webhook testing then silently targets a dead tunnel.
response.explanation: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:68 runs `sed -i '' -E ...` when GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL already exists in the env file. This is macOS/BSD syntax. GNU sed treats the empty string as the script and then fails to parse the real expression, so the URL is never updated. The script still prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL" afterward, because nothing checks sed's exit status. The failure and error paths also call cleanup, which does `exit 0`, so they report success.
response.title: BSD-only `sed -i ''` breaks the env update on Linux

response.consequence: Users can no longer trigger the recording check for past Cal Video bookings that are not yet marked as recorded. The menu item shows greyed out, which is a functional regression of an existing feature.
response.explanation: Before the change, a past, confirmed Cal Video booking with no recording (`showCheckRecordingButton`) got an enabled "check_for_recordings" button that opened ViewRecordingsDialog. The refactor drops `showCheckRecordingButton`. `getVideoOptionsActions` always labels the action `view_recordings`. BookingListItem also adds `(action.id === "view_recordings" && !booking.isRecorded)` to `disabled`. So for any booking where `isRecorded` is false, the action is permanently disabled and the dialog cannot be opened. That is exactly the case the old "check for recordings" button handled, for example a recording that has not been synced yet. `getVideoOptionsActions` and `isActionDisabled` also now show session details and recordings under different conditions than before. For example, the old code gated recordings on `isConfirmed`, while `isActionDisabled` checks `status === ACCEPTED`. A second, smaller difference: the confirm-button condition in `getPendingActions` uses `showPendingPayment && booking.paid`, which can never be true because `showPendingPayment` requires `!booking.paid`. It also dropped the `price` check, so a payment-enabled booking with no payment rows now gets a Confirm button.
response.title: "Check for recordings" flow removed: view_recordings is disabled for unrecorded Cal Video bookings

response.consequence: For a response whose routed booking is created after the response is saved, the denormalized row never gets its booking status, times, user, event type or UTM data. Analytics and filters on that table show those responses as having no booking, and the row is wrong until the response is next updated. A changed booking user also leaves the old name, email and avatar in the row.
response.explanation: The booking trigger function updates RoutingFormResponseDenormalized only `WHERE rfrd."bookingId" = NEW.id`. A denormalized row gets `bookingId` only when the refresh function finds the booking through `b.uid = r."routedToBookingUid"`. If the form response is saved before the booking row exists, the refresh inserts the row with `bookingId` NULL. When the booking is later inserted, `booking_insert_trigger_for_routing_form` runs this function, but the WHERE clause matches no rows. The function also never sets `bookingUid` or `bookingId`. It never sets `bookingUserName`, `bookingUserEmail` or `bookingUserAvatarUrl`, so those columns stay stale after a booking `userId` change. Tracking and assignment-reason rows are also not copied in, because their triggers use the same `bookingId` match.
response.title: Booking insert/update trigger cannot link denormalized rows that were created before the booking existed

response.consequence: Clients get a misleading 500 and the server logs it as an internal error for an expected user-input condition. Team admins cannot clear the cache for team-owned credentials.
response.explanation: The route is registered with authedProcedure and validates credentialId as z.number(), and the handler scopes the lookup to userId === ctx.user.id. So there is no authorization bypass, and a client cannot delete another user's cache. The handler throws a plain `Error` when the credential is not found or not owned. tRPC maps non-TRPCError exceptions to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so a missing or foreign credentialId returns a 500, not NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN. The handler also only matches credentials whose userId is the caller, so team or delegation credentials (null userId) cannot have their cache cleared. I did not confirm whether the UI shows the cache action for those credentials.
response.title: Plain Error for missing/unauthorized credential yields 500 instead of NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN
